intro: Convert terabytes (TB) into gigabytes (GB) accurately for external hard drives, NAS storage pools, SSD upgrades, and cloud backup plans. Under the SI decimal standard used by drive makers, there are 1,000 gigabytes in 1 terabyte—to turn any TB to gigabyte capacity, multiply terabytes by 1,000. Compare decimal capacity against binary OS reporting and scan sizes from 0.5 TB to 500 TB below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Decimal TB (1,000 GB) vs. Binary TiB (1,024 GiB) & Power Units (TW to GW)
items: Drive makers and cloud billing define 1 TB as 1,000 GB (10¹² bytes), whereas Windows reports binary gibibytes (1,024³ bytes) under the 'GB' label—so a 1 TB drive displays ~931 GB and an 8 TB drive displays ~7,450 GB.
While both terabytes (TB → GB) and terawatts (TW → GW) share the 1,000× SI prefix step, TB/GB measure digital data capacity whereas TW/GW measure electrical power.

faqs.question: How many gigabytes (GB) are in 1 terabyte (TB)?
faqs.answer: There are 1,000 gigabytes (GB) in 1 decimal terabyte (TB) under the international SI standard used by storage manufacturers. In binary computing (tebibytes), 1 TiB equals 1,024 GiB.

faqs.question: How do you convert terabytes to gigabytes?
faqs.answer: Multiply the number of terabytes by 1,000: GB = TB × 1,000. For example, an 8 TB hard drive equals 8 × 1,000 = 8,000 GB decimal.

faqs.question: What is 10 TB in GB?
faqs.answer: 10 terabytes equals 10,000 gigabytes (10 × 1,000 = 10,000 GB) in decimal storage—or about 9,313 GiB when formatted in binary OS units.

faqs.question: What is 500 TB in GB?
faqs.answer: 500 terabytes equals 500,000 gigabytes (500 × 1,000 = 500,000 GB) under the SI decimal standard.
